name: The Baltimore Sun editorial board
lean_basis: AllSides rates The Baltimore Sun Center (low confidence, Oct. 2026) and Ad Fontes rates it Middle. Largest Maryland daily, bought in January 2024 by Sinclair executive chairman David Smith with Armstrong Williams; Williams said that month the Sun 'will stop endorsing political candidates' (Baltimore Banner, Jan. 20, 2024). Its opinion pages have run guest pieces against Question 3, but no board position was found, and no Sun editorial on Baltimore City Questions A to I was found (the site blocks automated reads).

name: The Baltimore Banner
lean_basis: AllSides rates The Baltimore Banner Center (independent review, low or initial confidence, as of Oct. 2026). As a 501(c)(3) newsroom it does not endorse candidates or ballot questions.

name: League of Women Voters of Baltimore City
lean_basis: League of Women Voters chapter; its page describes the League as 'a nonpartisan political organization' (https://my.lwv.org/maryland/baltimore-city). No outside rating found; lean reflects its stated mission.

name: Maryland Democratic Party
lean_basis: Official state party organization; backs its nominees and campaigns for Question 3 (chair Steuart Pittman). No Baltimore City Democratic Party 2026 slate page was found (its site's vote page is stale 2020 content).

name: Maryland Republican Party
lean_basis: Official state party organization; backs its nominees. Runs the 'Save Our Voice' campaign to defeat Question 3. No Baltimore City Republican slate was found.

name: Sierra Club Maryland Chapter PAC
lean_basis: AllSides rates the national Sierra Club Lean Left (think tank/policy group; independent review, low or initial confidence, as of Oct. 2026). This is its Maryland chapter.

name: Baltimore Mayor Brandon M. Scott
lean_basis: Democratic mayor of Baltimore; national co-chair of Mayors for Guaranteed Income.

name: Baltimore City Council President Zeke Cohen
lean_basis: Democratic City Council president; backed the charter package that became Questions E, F and G, and co-announced Question H.

name: Baltimore City Comptroller Bill Henry
lean_basis: Democratic city comptroller and Board of Estimates member.

name: Gov. Wes Moore
lean_basis: Democratic governor of Maryland (on the ballot for re-election).

name: State Sen. Antonio Hayes
lean_basis: Democratic state senator for District 40 (on the ballot for re-election).

name: Baltimore Teachers Union
lean_basis: Teachers' union for Baltimore City schools, an AFT affiliate (https://www.baltimoreteachers.org/about). Its page gives no mission text, and unions map to lean_left (workers' bargaining power and labor rights). No outside rating found; lean reflects its stated mission.

name: Metropolitan Baltimore Council of AFL-CIO Unions
lean_basis: AFL-CIO central labor council for the Baltimore area. Its site (https://www.metrobaltimoreaflcio.org/) could not be read on Oct. 17, 2026, and unions map to lean_left (workers' bargaining power and labor rights). No outside rating found; lean reflects its stated mission.

name: 1199SEIU United Healthcare Workers East
lean_basis: Healthcare workers' union whose stated mission is 'to stand up for quality healthcare, good jobs and social justice for all' (https://www.1199seiu.org/about). No outside rating found; lean reflects its stated mission.

name: Progressive Maryland
lean_basis: Self-described progressive group that says it is 'leading the fight for progressive change in Maryland' (https://www.progressivemaryland.org/about). No outside rating found; lean reflects its stated mission.

name: Greater Baltimore Democratic Socialists of America
lean_basis: Local chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America; it works 'for a socialist future in Greater Baltimore' (https://baltimoredsa.org/). No outside rating found; lean reflects its stated mission.

name: Charm City Indivisible
lean_basis: Baltimore chapter of the Indivisible movement that describes itself as 'building political power to strengthen democracy and advance justice in our city and beyond' (https://charmcityindivisible.org/). No outside rating found; lean reflects its stated mission.

name: Moms Demand Action / Everytown 'Gun Sense Candidate'
lean_basis: Gun-safety group, part of Everytown for Gun Safety, that calls itself 'a grassroots movement of Americans fighting for public safety measures that can protect people from gun violence' (https://momsdemandaction.org/about/). No outside rating found; lean reflects its stated mission.

name: Baltimore Baby Fund campaign
lean_basis: Ballot committee for Question I only (a joint campaign with Mayor Scott). A single-measure committee has no general ideological mission, so 'neutral' here means not assessed.
